tools.name: verify-email
tools.title: Verify Email
tools.description: Verify a single email address with Bouncer. Returns Bouncer's status (deliverable, risky, undeliverable or unknown), its reason code, a score out of 100, the mail provider and MX record, and every domain and account signal with the value Bouncer reported for it. Does not include a send-or-suppress recommendation. Spends one Bouncer credit per address.

tools.name: verify-domain
tools.title: Verify Domain
tools.description: Check a domain with Bouncer. Bouncer's domain endpoint returns no status or score — only the mail record it found, the provider, and whether the domain is catch-all, disposable, free or toxic. Use this when asked about a domain rather than a specific mailbox. Spends one Bouncer credit.

tools.name: get-credits
tools.title: Get Bouncer Credits
tools.description: Get the number of Bouncer verification credits remaining on the account. Does not spend a credit.

ai.instructions:
- Each verify-email or verify-domain call spends one Bouncer credit. Verify only what the user asked about, and never re-verify something you already have a result for in this conversation.
- Report what Bouncer returned. These tools deliberately do not include a send-or-suppress recommendation, so do not present one as though it came from Bouncer; if the user asks whether to send, say the judgement is theirs and give them the fields it rests on.
- A signal value of "Unknown" means Bouncer could not determine it. Never report it as "No", and never treat it as evidence either way.
- The roleAddress and freeProvider signals are heuristics over the local part and the domain, and they misfire on personal addresses such as mail@ or contact@. Report them as observations, not defects.
- The domain endpoint returns no status or score, only the fields listed. Do not infer whether a domain can receive mail beyond what those fields say.
- When didYouMean is returned, surface the suggested correction and offer to verify it instead.
- If a call fails because the account is out of credits, say so plainly and stop; do not retry.
